description: Coverage measurement infrastructure issue discovered: Swift 6.3 + Swift Testing framework causes profraw files to not capture XCTest test execution properly when --enable-code-coverage is used with mixed XCTest/Swift Testing suites. Best confirmed coverage remains 28.1% from earlier runs. Added ~200 new tests across 7 test files covering SentimentClassifier, ToolPermissionSnapshot, BargeInDecisions, FalseInterruptionRecovery, BackchannelClassifier, LegacyThresholdInterruptionDecider, EchoSuppressor, VoiceTagStripper, and more.

hypothesis.toolchain_issue: Swift Testing framework (swift-testing) runs XCTest tests through swiftpm-testing-helper which may produce separate coverage data. The profraw merge captures only partial execution. This is a known Swift 6 issue with mixed XCTest/Swift Testing suites.
hypothesis.recommendation_for_team: Run 'xcodebuild test -scheme Fae -destination platform=macOS -enableCodeCoverage YES' for accurate coverage measurement, or use 'swift test --enable-code-coverage' with ONLY XCTest tests. The new tests are valid and compile — the measurement toolchain is the bottleneck.

description: Fixed coverage measurement: Swift 6.3 overwrites profraw files on each swift test run. Solution: accumulate profraws across per-suite filter runs by copying them to a temp directory before each run, then merge all at end. Coverage now reads 27.2% (32,501/119,699 lines), close to baseline 27.8%. 189 files covered, 109 zero-cov. Takes ~7.5min per run.

hypothesis.root_cause: SwiftPM names profraw files deterministically by binary hash + PID. Each swift test run overwrites previous profraws.
hypothesis.fix: Copy profraws to temp dir after each --filter run, merge all at end
hypothesis.next_action_hint: Optimize runtime by batching suites. Then add more tests to improve coverage from 27.2% toward 90%.
